beats.hook: I quit my job in the middle of a client presentation. No notice. No two weeks. I just stood up, said "I'm done," and walked out.
beats.normal_life: I had worked at that marketing agency for four years. My manager, Derek, always took credit for my campaigns — but I told myself that was just how it worked.
beats.first_red_flag: Then one Tuesday, I overheard Derek on the phone. He was pitching my entire Q4 strategy — word for word — to a headhunter. As his own work. For a job at a competitor.
beats.the_reveal: That presentation he made me run that afternoon? It was for the competitor's board. He was auditioning. Using my slides. With my name stripped off every single page.
beats.aftermath: I stood up mid-slide, looked Derek dead in the eye, and said — "This campaign was mine. Good luck explaining that without me." Then I walked out. HR called the next day. So did Derek's new employer, after Derek's offer got pulled. Turns out the competitor wanted to verify the work. Derek couldn't answer a single question about it. I got a consulting offer from that same company two weeks later.
beats.cta: Would you have stayed and fought from the inside — or walked out exactly like I did? Drop it below.
